content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "For each firm, compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using annual data lagged at least 4 months. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "When inventory builds faster than sales, it signals overproduction and weakening demand that management has not yet recognized, presaging future markdowns and disappointing earnings.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)"}, {"name": "Accrual Reversal Score", "construction": "Compute total accruals as (change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities excluding debt minus depreciation) scaled by average total assets, from Compustat balance-sheet items. Rank firms into deciles annually.", "rationale": "High accruals reflect low-quality, less persistent earnings that mean-revert, so market participants over-extrapolate accrual-driven earnings and are subsequently disappointed.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (low accruals)"}, {"name": "Analyst Coverage Neglect", "construction": "Count the number of I/B/E/S analysts issuing FY1 EPS estimates in the most recent month, orthogonalized against log market capitalization via cross-sectional regression; take the residual. Low residual = neglected relative to size.", "rationale": "Stocks under-followed relative to their size are less efficiently priced and carry an information/neglect premium that resolves as coverage catches up.", "higher_returns_for": "low residual coverage (neglected firms)"}, {"name": "Gross Profitability to Assets", "construction": "Compute (revenue minus cost of goods sold) from Compustat (SALE minus COGS) divided by total assets (AT), using annual data lagged 4+ months. Sort into deciles.", "rationale": "Gross profit is a cleaner measure of economic productivity than bottom-line earnings and captures profitable firms whose value is not fully reflected in price.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Cash Flow Volatility Discount", "construction": "Compute the standard deviation of quarterly operating cash flow (approximated by net income plus depreciation, items IBQ + DPQ) scaled by total assets over the trailing 20 quarters. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Firms with more stable cash flows are less risky and easier to value, but investors under-price the persistence advantage of low-volatility cash generators.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (stable cash flows)"}, {"name": "Order Flow Momentum from Volume-Weighted Signs", "construction": "Using daily CRSP data, sum signed daily dollar volume (volume times the sign of the daily return times price) over the trailing 3 months, scaled by average dollar volume. Rank into deciles monthly.", "rationale": "Persistent net buying pressure reflects gradual information incorporation and institutional accumulation that continues over subsequent months.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (positive net buying pressure)"}, {"name": "Debt Maturity Rollover Risk", "construction": "Compute the ratio of debt in current liabilities (Compustat DLC) to total debt (DLC + DLTT). Rank firms; higher ratio means more short-term debt requiring near-term refinancing.", "rationale": "Firms with heavy near-term refinancing needs bear rollover and liquidity risk, demanding a return premium, especially in tightening credit environments.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (more short-term debt reliance)"}, {"name": "Sales-to-Price Efficiency", "construction": "Compute annual sales (SALE) divided by market capitalization (CRSP price times shares). Sort into deciles, lagging accounting data 4+ months.", "rationale": "Sales are harder to manipulate than earnings, so a high sales-to-price ratio identifies fundamentally cheap firms whose revenue base the market undervalues.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Intensity Reversal", "construction": "Compute capital expenditures (CAPX) scaled by lagged total assets, then subtract the firm's trailing 3-year average of the same ratio. Rank the deviation cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Abnormal investment surges tend to reflect empire-building and over-optimism that erode future returns on capital, disappointing investors.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (below-normal investment)"}, {"name": "Earnings Announcement Return Persistence", "construction": "Cumulate the abnormal (market-adjusted) CRSP return over the 3-day window around each of the four most recent quarterly earnings announcements, and average them. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Consistently positive market reactions to earnings news reflect a pattern of positive surprises that the market underweights, leading to continued outperformance.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (consistently positive announcement reactions)"}]}
